title: Sharpness-aware Model Merging with Salience Recovery for LLM-based Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: LLM-based cross-domain sequential recommendation faces cross-domain knowledge conflict and performance saturation during multi-domain fusion.

gap.claim: Model merging requires mechanisms that address parameter-level misalignment and statistical homogenization.

contributions.claim: SharpRec is a framework for sharpness-aware model merging with salience recovery in LLM-based cross-domain sequential recommendation.
Sharpness-aware Geometric Alignment establishes a stable geometric foundation for interference-free fusion.
Preference Salience Activation recovers distinctive features intended to improve target-domain performance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments were conducted in dual-domain and multi-domain scenarios.
SharpRec consistently outperformed state-of-the-art baselines according to the authors.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs support cross-domain sequential recommendation through semantic reasoning without relying on overlapping users.
Model merging is presented as scalable and flexible for integrating knowledge across domains, but exhibits conflict and saturation.
The abstract attributes these bottlenecks to parameter-level misalignment and statistical homogenization.
SharpRec combines geometric alignment with preference salience activation.
The authors report consistent superiority over state-of-the-art baselines across dual-domain and multi-domain settings.

source_observation.claim: Model merging can suffer from knowledge conflict and performance saturation during multi-domain fusion.

interpretation.claim: Merging diverse domain knowledge may require both alignment of parameter geometry and preservation of domain-distinctive features.

application.claim: For multi-domain model fusion, consider separating interference reduction from recovery of target-relevant salience.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition generalizes beyond the reported recommendation settings.
